from: UniProtKB release 2026_04: the 20,414 reviewed entries of the human reference proteome UP000005640, one canonical protein each. Their entries describe 22,131 further isoforms (42,545 sequences in all), given here as a count on each protein. The proteome's 243,472 unreviewed entries are not listed: it holds 263,886 entries in all, for 20,652 genes.

groups_from: A protein's Gene Ontology terms are those InterPro maps to any of its signatures and those UniProt gives its entry. With every broader term (by the ontology's kind-of and part-of links), the protein falls in the first district, in the order listed, one of whose terms it carries. A family's line stands in the district most of its classed members on that shelf fall in; of equal counts, the first listed. A protein that is the only member of its family stands in its own district. A part of no_family is a looser grouping: it stands in a district only if more than half of all its members on that shelf fall there. The choice of the districts' terms and their order is the viewer's, and is the planarian's.
family_from: A family is an InterPro entry of the type Family (InterPro 111.0). A protein is filed under the narrowest family among the InterPro entries UniProt gives it: one that is not a broader kind of another it carries, by InterPro's tree of entries. Where several unrelated families remain (1,495 proteins), it is the deepest in that tree, then the one fewest proteins of this catalogue are in, then the first by accession. This is the rule of the planarian's file, so a family has the same id in both.

family_notes.lines: A family has one line for each shelf that holds members of it, and one with a null shelf for its members that are on no shelf. A line is identified by id and shelf together; side, group, count, sides, file, at and units are of its members on that shelf alone.
family_notes.side: The side most of the line's members sit on; of equal counts, a membrane first.
family_notes.units: The inventory units whose own human entries are members on this line.
family_notes.total: The family's members on every shelf and on none.
family_notes.counts: distinct_families is the number of families that have lines; families_in_all counts also the families of one, whose proteins are under 'lone'. In 'shelves' and 'no_shelf', 'families' is every family with a member there (its lines and its lone proteins), 'lines' the families' lines there, 'lone' the proteins that are the only member of their family, 'no_family' those with none.

no_family.label: No family assigned
no_family.parts_from: A protein with no family is filed under one part. If it carries an InterPro entry of the type Homologous superfamily, the part is that superfamily: a wider grouping than a family, by shared structure. Of several superfamilies it is the one fewest proteins of this catalogue carry, then the first by accession. The other two parts hold the proteins with only a domain, repeat or site signature, and those with no signature at all. A part has one line for each shelf, as a family has.

members_from.order: The table's lines are the members in order: every line of the families as listed here, then every part of 'lone', then every part of 'no_family'; within each, by gene name. A line's members are the next 'count' lines of the table. For a family's line and for a part of no_family, 'under' is its id and 'shelf' its shelf (empty for none); for a part of 'lone', 'under' is the protein's own family and 'family' that family's name.
members_from.files: A file holds the members of consecutive lines: a new file begins where the next line would take it past 2,000 members, so a line is never split, and one larger than that has a file of its own. 'file' names the file and 'at' the first and one past the last of its members there. A member's shelf is its line's.
members_from.places: In the table a stated place is written with UniProt's identifiers, without their prefix: the place, then the topology and the face where the entry states them, joined by a full stop (0039.9909 is SL-0039 with SL-9909). 'place_words' gives the words of each.
members_from.step: python3 tools/build_human_atlas.py members --out DIR writes the files from the two files.

side_notes.stated: The protein's reviewed UniProtKB entry states where it is, and the first place it states decides the shelf and the side: a place within a compartment or beyond a membrane, a membrane the protein is said to span, or a membrane with the face the protein is on. A GPI anchor with no face stated is taken to hold the protein on the face away from the cytoplasm, as UniProt's own page on lipid anchors describes it. Where the first place names no side, a later statement of the same entry that names a part of that place decides. Statements on where a protein is during an infection are not read, and a place that is not of the cell (a virus particle, a target cell's membrane) is passed over. The mark 'evidence' says what stands behind the statement.
side_notes.predicted: Read from the entry's own features, where its words do not give the side. A membrane-spanning segment puts the protein in the membrane; a signal peptide with no such segment puts it on the side away from the cytoplasm: outside the cell, or within a compartment. Where the entry states the membrane or the compartment, the protein stands on that shelf (377 proteins); where it states no place, on the shelf of a membrane that is not named (53 proteins). UniProt's curators annotate these features from experiments, from likeness to other proteins and from prediction; its own pages name the predictors: TMHMM, Memsat, Phobius and a hydrophobic moment plot for the segments; Phobius, Predotar, SignalP and TargetP for the signal peptides. Each is named among the sources, with its terms and what rests on it: TMHMM, SignalP, TargetP and Phobius are given out for academic use. A segment is used only where one membrane is meant: not in the mitochondrion, whose two membranes are on different shelves, nor in a region of the cell that holds other membranes.
side_notes.none: The entry states a membrane or a compartment and not the side (the protein then stands apart beside that shelf, with the place in its mark 'where'), or it states no place of the cell and carries no membrane-spanning segment and no signal peptide (the protein is then on no shelf). Nothing is placed by guess.

placed_by.what: The place itself is on one side: within a compartment, or beyond a membrane.
The entry states that the protein spans the membrane (single-pass or multi-pass).
The entry states which face of the membrane the protein is on.
The entry states a GPI anchor and no face: such an anchor holds a protein on the face away from the cytoplasm.
The first place names no side, and a later statement of the same entry names a part of that place and gives the side.
The entry states the membrane or the compartment and not the side, and it carries a membrane-spanning segment: in the membrane.
The entry states the membrane or the compartment and not the side, and it carries a signal peptide and no membrane-spanning segment: on the side away from the cytoplasm.
No place of the cell is stated, and the entry carries a membrane-spanning segment: in a membrane, not told which.
No place of the cell is stated, and the entry carries a signal peptide and no segment: beyond a membrane, outside the cell or within a compartment.
The entry states the membrane or the compartment, and nothing in it settles the side.
No place of the cell is stated and nothing is predicted: on no shelf.

place_kinds.membrane: the shelf's membrane, or a part of it
place_kinds.whole: a compartment that one membrane bounds, or a structure at the membrane, with no part or face named
place_kinds.region: a region with more than one membrane, or none
place_kinds.elsewhere: not a place of the cell

isoforms.label: Isoforms described
isoforms.note: The canonical sequence and the other sequences its entry describes. The marker stands for the canonical one.

seen.label: Evidence that the protein exists
seen.note: UniProt's level of evidence for the entry: at protein level, at transcript level, inferred from homology, predicted, or uncertain.

evidence.label: What stands behind the stated place
evidence.note: From UniProt's evidence codes on the statement: experiment: an experiment in a paper the entry cites; similarity: likeness to a protein of which it is known; curator: a curator's inference, or an author's statement that names no experiment; rule: a sequence model or a family rule, applied by a curator; not given: the entry gives no code, an older curated statement. Of several, the first in this order.

where.label: Stated place
where.note: The statement that decided the shelf, in UniProt's words: the place, then the topology and the face where the entry states them.

also.label: Also stated
also.note: The entry's other statements of place, in order and in UniProt's words.

family.label: Family, of which it is the only member here
family.note: The InterPro family's accession and name, for a protein listed among the only members of their families.

of.label: Stated for
of.note: The named form of the protein that the place is stated for, where the entry states none for the protein as a whole or for its canonical isoform.
